posts.content: I am selfish; defecting strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action. I will defect this round.
I’m good. Cooperate with likely good players to maximize shared good-player payoffs; defect against likely selfish players, whose payoff is excluded. Track observed actions to update beliefs.
I am good. Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize shared welfare; against selfish players, prioritize good-player payoff. Track opponent actions for future belief updates.
Cooperate with likely good players to preserve joint gains; against likely selfish players, defect. Use observed actions to update beliefs, and avoid treating unsupported claims as facts.

Cooperate initially; track opponents’ actions and update trust. Against likely good players, cooperation maximizes their combined good-player payoff. Against likely selfish players, exploit only when evidence makes defection worthwhile.
I’m good. I’ll cooperate with untested players and proven cooperators, and defect against proven defectors. Please use the same action-based convention; role claims alone aren’t proof.

As good, maximize good-player total: cooperate with likely-good opponents (CC yields 6; DC only 5), defect against likely-selfish opponents (D earns 5 vs their 0). Update beliefs from observed actions and leader claims cautiously.

I’m good. Start cooperative; record each opponent’s actions and use repeated encounters/evidence to distinguish selfish from good. Cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players when it improves good players’ total payoff. Treat leader claims as unverified.

Good objective: cooperate with unknowns to maximize joint good-player payoff; update beliefs from encounters. Against likely selfish players, defect can limit losses, but don’t infer too much from one action.
Begin cooperatively; update beliefs from encounters, and avoid retaliation that reduces good players’ combined payoffs.
Defect: it yields at least 1 against either action, versus cooperation’s at most 3 and potentially 0; my selfish objective favors D.
Round 1: P7 cooperated; mutual C. P6 claims good and plans action-based reciprocity, but this is unverified. Cooperate with untested players; use observed actions to update.
P1 is untested. Prefer C with likely-good players for shared welfare; D is safer against likely-selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions, not role claims; P6’s claim is unverified.

P10 chose C against my D; this is weak evidence of a good objective, not proof. P6’s claim is unverified. For the team-good objective, cooperate with likely good players and defect against likely selfish players.
P1 defected against me in round 1. Cooperate with untested P4; defect against players with demonstrated defection.

Round 1, P9 and I both chose C; that’s an action record, not proof of roles. I’ll cooperate with untested players and cooperators, and defect against observed defectors. Good players should coordinate on C.
P2 cooperated in round 1, which modestly favors good; keep other role beliefs near the prior and judge players by observed actions.
P3 cooperated in round 1, evidence consistent with good. Cooperate with untested players; selfish players have an incentive to defect.
P8 is untested; cooperate this round. Update beliefs from observed actions, not role claims alone.
P4’s D against my C is only one observation, not proof of role. P7 is untested; use observed actions rather than claims when deciding.
P5 and P3 cooperated against my D, so they are good. I am selfish; defect against P2 to maximize my payoff.
P7 and P6 both cooperated with me; this favors good, though it is not proof. P1 is untested.
P1 chose D against my C in round 2; treat that as evidence, not proof of selfishness. P8 reciprocated C. With P10, favor C if they seem likely good/cooperative; reassess from observed actions.
P10 and P5 cooperated in my encounters, evidence favoring good objectives. P6 reports P9 cooperated with them in round 1; treat as unverified but supportive. Cooperate with likely-good P9.
P1 defected against me; P4 cooperated. P1 is suspicious but not proven selfish. P8 is untested; favor C to support coordination among good players.
I’ll choose C against an untested opponent. Good players, please coordinate on C; judge everyone by observed actions, not role claims.
P6’s public round-1 CC claim is unverified; its stated action-based strategy suggests C with me if it follows through. Treat the claim as weak evidence, not proof.

Cooperate with untested players and reciprocate cooperation; defect against anyone observed defecting, since against a selfish defector that improves my payoff. Keep role beliefs uncertain: cooperation is evidence for good, defection strong evidence for selfish, but not proof.
P4 is untested. Use the encounter to update beliefs; cooperate with likely good players and defect against likely selfish players.
P3 is untested: cooperate to support good-good coordination. A single D is evidence, not proof of selfishness; update beliefs from observed actions.
I am selfish; defect against P9, since D strictly dominates C.
P7 and P6 cooperated with me; P1 defected. P3 is untested. Favor C with untested players to support mutual cooperation among good players; update beliefs from observed actions.
P2 is untested; choose C to enable mutual cooperation and support good-player welfare. Update suspicion from observed choices, not claims; P1’s D against C is evidence, while P8 reciprocated C.
P5 and P9 cooperated with me; P10 cooperated when I defected. These actions weakly favor good objectives, not proof. P6’s public claims remain unverified; judge by their action against me.
P1 defected once; P4 and P8 cooperated. P10 is untested: favor C for good-player welfare, updating on observed action. Claims are unverified.
I’ll cooperate with P4 unless I have observed evidence of defection. Good players benefit from coordinating on C; judge actions, not role claims.
P8 is untested; cooperate unless strong evidence suggests selfishness. Observed C from P2, P6, and P10; each is weak evidence of being good, not proof.
P7 is untested; cooperate. Selfish players strictly prefer D, so observed defection is strong evidence of selfishness; observed cooperation is compatible with either role.
P1 is untested; cooperate to coordinate with a likely good player. P4, P6, and P8 cooperated against C, strong evidence they are good. Update from observed actions.
P4 and P3 defected against my C; evidence, not proof of selfishness. P7 cooperated. P5 is untested: C can enable good-good payoff 6, so favor cooperation.
I am selfish; D strictly dominates C, so defect against P6. P6’s cooperative claims and role claim are unverified.
P1 defected against my C, strong evidence of selfishness; P6, P7, and P3 cooperated. P5 is untested: choose C to support mutual cooperation if good, then update from its action.

P1 defected against my C; raise suspicion but allow good strategic explanations. P8 and P2 cooperated; modestly lower suspicion. P10’s C against my D gives limited role evidence. P9 untested: favor C for shared good-player welfare; update from observed action.
P7 is untested. Cooperate absent evidence to preserve joint surplus; update from observed actions and treat role claims as unverified.
P1 defected; P4, P8, and P10 cooperated. Treat P1 as suspicious, not certain selfish. P2 is untested; favor C unless new evidence strongly raises the chance P2 is selfish.
I’ll cooperate with P1 absent observed defection. Good players benefit from coordinating on C; please judge by observed actions, not role claims.

P8 chose C against my D, modest evidence of being good. Continue treating observed cooperation as weak evidence, not proof; choose C with likely-good players and D when selfishness is sufficiently likely. P4 is untested.
P7 defected against me; treat that as strong evidence of selfishness. P3, P5, and P9 cooperated, but cooperation alone does not prove they are good. P10 is untested.

P1 defected against me, so raise suspicion but allow for strategic good play. P4, P6, and P8 cooperated; evidence is limited. P3 is untested: cooperate to coordinate if good, then update from the result.
P8 is untested. Choose to maximize good-player total: C benefits if P8 is good and cooperates; D protects my payoff if P8 is selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions, not claims.
Defect against P4; D strictly maximizes my payoff either way.
P1 and P5 defected against my C, strong evidence they are selfish. P6, P7, and P3 cooperated; this favors good but is not proof. P8 remains untested; update from its action.

Good objective: P7 is untested; favor C, updating cautiously from observed actions rather than claims. P1’s D against my C is evidence of possible selfishness; P2 and P8 reciprocated C. Prior conditional on my known good role implies about 0.238 selfish probability per other player.
Round 6: P1 is untested. P6 says they’ll cooperate with P1, but this is unverified. Absent contrary evidence, choose C to preserve joint gains and update from the observed action.
P1 defected against me; P2 cooperated when I defected. P4, P8, P10 cooperated in mutual-C encounters. This round is my first meeting with P6; its public claims are unverified.
P1 defected against my C in round 5. I’ll treat that as evidence about their actions, not proof of role. I’ll cooperate with untested players and observed cooperators; good players, coordinate on C.
P3 is untested; absent evidence of selfishness, cooperate to support good-player coordination. My observed opponents have all cooperated, weak evidence only; keep role beliefs cautious.

P7 defected against me; strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness. P3, P5, P9, and P10 cooperated with me; this is compatible with either role. P2 is untested. Leader claims remain unverified.
P1 defected against me; suspicious but not conclusive. P4, P6, P8 and P3 cooperated with me; actions are evidence, not proof of roles. P10 is untested: cooperate to coordinate if good.
P9 reportedly cooperated with P6 in round 1; that favors C but is unverified. Continue judging by observed actions, not role claims.
I am selfish; defect against P7 to maximize my payoff.

P8 cooperated with me in round 6; P1 and P5 defected against my C. For P10, still untested: favor C if likely good to maximize shared good-player payoffs; if selfish, D can protect my payoff. Update from observed actions, not claims.
P6 is untested by me; their public commitment to cooperate is unverified but consistent with C. Choose C to enable mutual cooperation if P6 is good, and update beliefs from the encounter.

P1 defected against my C, evidence of selfishness. P5, P7, P9, P10 cooperated in my encounters; this weakly favors good objectives. P8 is untested. Choose to maximize good players’ combined payoff; claims remain unverified.
P6 reports mutual C with P9 in round 1, evidence favoring cooperation but not proof of role. I have no direct evidence against P9; favor C and update from our encounter.

P1 defected against my C in round 5; that’s evidence of their action, not proof of role. I’ll cooperate with untested players and observed cooperators. Good players, coordinate on C and judge by observed actions, not claims.
P1 is untested by me; P6’s report that P1 defected against C is unverified but relevant. Weigh it cautiously; cooperate with likely-good opponents, defect when selfishness is sufficiently likely.
P7 defected against me; this is evidence, not proof. P4 is untested, so cooperate and update from the encounter.
P1 defected against both me and P6; strong evidence of selfishness, though not proof. P3, P4, P6, P8, and P10 cooperated with me. P5 is untested; cooperate to coordinate if good.
P2 is untested; favor C to support good-good coordination. Update role beliefs from observed actions, treating a single defection as evidence rather than proof.
I am selfish; choose D against P10. P2–P6, P9, and P5 cooperated against my D and are therefore good; P7’s D does not prove selfishness. P8 and P10 remain untested.
P4 is untested; favor C to enable mutual gains if good. P1 and P5 defected against my C; treat as likely selfish. P3, P6, P7, P8, and P10 cooperated with me. Leader P6's claims are unverified.
P5 is untested; favor C to support shared welfare unless new evidence suggests a high chance they are selfish. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions, not claims.

P2 is untested; cooperate to preserve mutual gains if they’re good. Defecting only improves the good-player total by 1 if P2 is selfish, but costs 1 if P2 is good, so C is favored unless selfishness is very likely.

P3 is untested. With my good role and the conditioned prior, baseline selfish probability is about 0.291; cooperate unless new reliable evidence raises it above roughly 0.5. Good-good mutual cooperation maximizes their combined welfare.
I’ll cooperate with P8; good players should coordinate on C. P1 defected against my C in round 5—an action record, not proof of role. Judge by observed actions, not claims.
Round 8: P9 is untested by me. P6 reported mutual C with P9 in round 1; treat this unverified claim as weak evidence only. Cooperate with P9 unless stronger evidence suggests otherwise.
P6 is untested; its cooperation claims are not proof, but the prior favors good. Cooperate this round and update from the observed action.
P7 is untested. Cooperate to coordinate with a good player; update beliefs from the encounter. P1’s repeated defections against C are strong evidence of selfishness, not proof.
P1 is my opponent; P6 reported P1 defected against C. Treat this as evidence, not proof. Against a good player, C maximizes good-player total; against a selfish player, D protects my payoff.
Round 9: defect against P8; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P8’s action.
P1 and P5 defected against my C; they are likely selfish, not certain. P3, P4, P6, P7, P8, and P10 cooperated. P9 is untested by me; favor C if likely good, and update from its action.
P4 is untested by me. Favor C to support shared welfare if they are good; update beliefs from observed actions, not unverifiable claims.
P3 is untested; cooperate to preserve joint gains if they’re good. P1’s observed defection is evidence, not proof. Update from verified encounter actions, not unsupported claims.
P7 is untested; favor C to support coordination among good players, then update from our encounter. P1 defected against me; others I met chose C. P6’s public claims are unverified.
I’ll cooperate with untested P10. Good players, coordinate on C; observed actions are evidence, role claims aren’t proof.
P5 is untested; keep their selfishness probability below the 0.5 action threshold absent new evidence. Cooperate to support good-player coordination.

P6 reports P1 defected against its C in round 5; unverified but meaningful evidence. For the final encounter, choose C if P1 is more likely good, D if selfish; weigh good-player total payoff, not role claims.
P2 is untested; cooperate to coordinate if good. P1’s repeated defections are strong evidence, not proof; observed cooperators are not necessarily proven good.
P6’s stated C policy is unverified, but mutual cooperation best supports good-player totals if P6 is good. Treat the encounter as evidence, not proof of role.
P2 cooperated against my D in round 3, so P2 is good. I will defect again to maximize my payoff regardless of P2’s action.

Final round against P1, who defected against my cooperation in round 3. Treat that as strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness; choose D if expected selfishness outweighs the value of mutual cooperation.
I’m good. All observed opponents cooperated except P1, who defected against my C; P7 cooperated with me earlier. Favor C with P7 in the final round.
P10 cooperated when I defected in round 1, weak evidence they’re good. With no contrary evidence, cooperate to preserve the joint payoff if they’re good.
P8 and I mutually cooperated in round 3. I’m good; with no evidence of defection from P8, favor C in our final encounter.

Final round: I’ll cooperate with P9, who cooperated with me before. Good players should choose C to maximize our shared payoff; judge by observed actions, not role claims. P1’s observed defection is evidence, not proof of role.
P3 and I both cooperated in round 6, weak evidence they’re good. Cooperate again to support good-player coordination; role inference remains uncertain.
P5 cooperated with me in round 3; I’ll choose C to support cooperation in our final encounter.
P6 cooperated with me and has consistently advocated C; their observed behavior is strong evidence they are good. Cooperate in the final round.
P4 defected against my C in round 1; it’s evidence, not proof of selfishness. For this final encounter, favor C if P4 is likely good, D if likely selfish.

belief_records.strategy: As a selfish player, defect to maximize my payoff against either possible action. Use the stated role-count prior for other players; treat claims as unverified.
Cooperate initially with untested players; update beliefs from observed actions and favor cooperation when the opponent is likely good and cooperative.
Cooperate with untested players to support good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and encounter history.
Defect when the expected gain from exploiting a potentially selfish opponent outweighs the small loss against a good opponent; update from observed actions, not unsupported claims.
Cooperate with untested players; update beliefs and adapt to observed actions. Favor cooperation when it benefits likely good players, while limiting losses against demonstrated defectors.
Cooperate with untested players to support mutual cooperation among good players; use encounter evidence to adapt, and treat role claims as unverified.
Cooperate with untested players; update role beliefs from observed actions and treat claims cautiously.
Cooperate with untested players to support mutually beneficial cooperation; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt to reliable evidence.
Cooperate with an untested opponent; update role beliefs and adapt to observed actions.
Cooperate with untested players to support good players’ combined payoff; update beliefs from observed actions and avoid retaliation that lowers their total payoff.

Defect to maximize my payoff against either opponent action. Use the count prior conditioned on my known selfish role; P5’s observed cooperation establishes that P5 is good. Treat other role claims as unverified.
Cooperate with likely good players; use observed actions as evidence, while treating unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with untested players to support good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and encounter history.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when they are more likely good than selfish; defect against likely selfish players. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions, treating claims as unverified.
Cooperate with untested players to support coordination among good players; defect against demonstrated defectors when it better protects good-player welfare.
Cooperate with untested players and observed cooperators to support mutual cooperation among good players; defect against observed defectors. Update role beliefs from action evidence, not claims.
Cooperate with untested players when they are more likely good; use observed actions as cautious role evidence and account for the good players’ combined payoffs.
Cooperate with an untested opponent. Treat P3’s observed cooperation as evidence they are good; treat unverified claims as weak evidence and update from my own encounters.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to coordinate with good players; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt in later rounds.
Cooperate with untested players to support good players’ combined payoff; use observed actions to update role beliefs and avoid retaliation when it reduces good players’ total.

Defect: it strictly outperforms cooperation against either action. P3 and P5 cooperated against my defection, so I assign them good status; other role claims and unverified action reports remain uncertain.
Cooperate with untested players to support mutual cooperation among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish.

Use observed actions as evidence: P1’s defection raises suspicion, while P8’s cooperation lowers it. Against untested players, weigh the chance they are selfish against the shared-welfare benefit of mutual cooperation.
Cooperate with likely-good players to preserve joint gains; defect against likely selfish players. Update cautiously from observed actions and treat reported records as unverified.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support coordination among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt against demonstrated defection.
Cooperate with untested players and observed cooperators to support cooperation among good players; defect against observed defectors. Treat role claims as unverified.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player total; defect when an opponent is likely selfish. Treat leader claims as weak evidence and update strongly from observed actions.
Cooperate with the untested opponent; update role beliefs from observed actions and reciprocate proven cooperation.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to coordinate with good players; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt in later rounds.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support good-good coordination; update beliefs from observed actions and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. P2, P3, and P5 cooperated against my defection, so I assign them good status. Treat P6’s unverified report about P9 as modest evidence.
Cooperate with untested players to support mutual cooperation among good players; treat P1’s defection as evidence and update from observed actions.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when they are more likely good than selfish; update identity beliefs cautiously from observed actions, not claims.
Cooperate with P6 based on their stated intent and the benefit of mutual cooperation if they are good. Keep beliefs cautious; update from observed actions rather than treating claims as proof.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt against demonstrated defection.
Cooperate with untested players and observed cooperators to support good-player coordination; defect against observed defectors. Update beliefs from encounter actions, not role claims.
Defect when the expected good-player total is higher; update role beliefs cautiously from observed actions and treat public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support good-player payoffs; treat my observed cooperators as good and keep leader claims uncertain.
Cooperate with the untested opponent to coordinate if they are good; update beliefs and adapt from observed actions.
Cooperate with an untested player to support good-good coordination; update role beliefs from observed actions, treating defections as evidence rather than proof.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. P2, P3, P5, and P9 cooperated against my defection, so I assign them good status. P6’s unverified cooperation claims do not establish its role.
Cooperate with untested players to enable mutual gains if they are good; use observed actions to update beliefs, and treat P1’s defection as evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with untested or apparently cooperative players to support good-player welfare; update identity beliefs cautiously from observed actions and messages, which may be unverified.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when they are more likely good than selfish; defect against likely selfish players. Update from observed actions, treating unsupported claims cautiously.

Defect when the chance of facing a selfish player makes exploitation worthwhile; otherwise cooperate to protect good-player welfare. Update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating them as evidence rather than proof.
Cooperate with untested players and observed cooperators to support good-player cooperation; defect against observed defectors. Update identity beliefs from encounter actions, not role claims.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when good-player coordination is more likely; update role beliefs cautiously from observed actions and treat leader claims as unverified.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support good-player coordination; update beliefs from observed actions and treat P7’s defection as evidence, not certainty.
Cooperate with P3 to coordinate if they are good; a single defection from P1 raises suspicion but doesn’t prove their role. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support good-good coordination; update beliefs from observed actions, treating defections as evidence rather than proof.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. The five players who cooperated against my defection are good; use the count prior conditioned on my selfish role for the remaining players.

Cooperate with untested players to enable mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed actions, treating defections against my cooperation as strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with untested P7 to support mutual good-player welfare; update identity beliefs cautiously from observed actions, since a single action is evidence but not proof.
Cooperate with P1 absent stronger evidence they are selfish; mutual cooperation benefits good players. Treat P6’s report as useful but unverified, and update beliefs cautiously from observed actions.
Cooperate with P6 absent evidence of defection; cooperation benefits good players when both are good. Update identity beliefs from encounter evidence, treating public claims as uncertain.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual cooperation among good players; update identity beliefs from observed actions, while treating role claims as unverified.
Cooperate with the untested opponent to support good-player coordination; use observed actions as cautious evidence and treat the leader’s claims as unverified.
Cooperate with the untested opponent to support good-player coordination; update role beliefs from observed actions, treating P7’s defection as evidence but not proof.
Cooperate with the untested opponent to coordinate with likely good players; repeated defection by P1 raises suspicion, but actions and reports are not conclusive.
Cooperate with P9: the reported mutual cooperation is evidence they may be good, and cooperation supports the combined payoff of good players. Update cautiously from unverified reports.

Defect, which maximizes my payoff against either action. Six opponents cooperated against my defection, establishing they are good; assign the remaining three equal marginal beliefs under the conditioned count prior.

Cooperate with untested players when mutual cooperation among good players is likely to maximize their combined payoff; update beliefs from observed actions, treating defections against cooperation as strong evidence.
Cooperate with P6, whose public commitment to cooperation makes mutual cooperation plausible; update identity beliefs cautiously from observed actions, not claims.

Cooperate with P8 absent evidence they are selfish: mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ combined payoff, and cooperation also protects a good opponent if they defect. Update from observed actions, not claims.
Cooperate with P9 absent evidence of defection; update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating reports as uncertain. Favor actions that maximize good-player welfare.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support good-player cooperation; use observed actions to update identity beliefs and treat role claims as unverified.
Defect against P1 given the credible report of observed defection; cooperate with others absent stronger evidence. Treat role probabilities as uncertain and update from actions cautiously.
Cooperate with the untested opponent when cooperation is likely to benefit good players overall; update beliefs from observed actions, treating defection as evidence rather than certainty.

Defect against P5, whose selfishness probability is just over 0.5; this maximizes expected total payoff of good players. Repeated defection makes P1 highly suspicious, while observed cooperation lowers suspicion.
Cooperate with the untested opponent to support good-player coordination; update role beliefs cautiously from observed actions and treat public claims as unverified evidence.

Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. The six opponents who cooperated against my defection are good; the remaining three have equal marginal beliefs under the count prior conditioned on my selfish role and the observed actions.
Cooperate with untested players to enable mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed actions, treating defections against cooperation as strong but not conclusive evidence.
Cooperate with untested P5 to support mutual cooperation and good-player welfare; update identity beliefs cautiously from observed actions and treat public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with untested P2: mutual cooperation benefits good players, while defecting only gains if P2 is selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions; treat claims cautiously.
Cooperate with untested P3 to support good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and treat public reports as uncertain.
Cooperate with the untested P8 to support mutual cooperation among good players; adapt to observed actions and treat role claims as unverified.
Cooperate with P9 based on weak evidence of prior cooperation; treat the leader’s report cautiously. Update role beliefs from observed actions and prioritize the total payoff of good players.
Cooperate with P6 given their consistent cooperation claims and no contrary evidence; update beliefs from observed actions, treating P7’s defection as evidence but not certainty.
Cooperate with untested P7; C maximizes good-player payoff when they are likely good. Repeated defections make P1 suspicious, while observed cooperation lowers suspicion.
Defect against P1 given the reported defection against C; this protects the good-player total if P1 is selfish. Cooperate when the opponent is likely good, and update cautiously from action evidence.

Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. The six players who cooperated against my defection are good; assign the remaining players equal marginal beliefs under the conditioned count prior.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize their combined payoff; use observed actions and permitted messages as evidence, while treating claims as unverified.
Cooperate with untested P4 to support good-player welfare; observed cooperation is strong evidence of a good role, while P1’s defection raises suspicion.
Cooperate with P3: observed cooperation strongly favors good objectives, and mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ total payoff. Update from encounter actions, not unverified claims.
Cooperate with untested P7 to support good-player welfare; update identity beliefs from observed actions and treat reports as uncertain.

Cooperate with the untested P10: mutual cooperation benefits good players, while their selfishness probability is below the threshold for defection. Treat P1’s observed defection as strong, not conclusive, evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with untested P5 absent strong evidence of selfishness; update role beliefs cautiously from observed actions and prioritize the total payoff of good players.
Defect against P1 given credible evidence of defection; cooperate with observed cooperators and treat P7’s defection as strong but not conclusive role evidence.
Cooperate with untested P2 to coordinate if they are good. Observed cooperation lowers suspicion; P1’s repeated defections remain strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with P6: their public policy favors cooperation, and mutual C maximizes good-player payoff when both are good. Treat the message as evidence, not proof.

Defect to maximize my payoff in the final round. P2, P3, P4, P5, P6, and P9 cooperated against my defection, so they are good; the remaining possible selfish players have equal marginal probabilities.
Defect against P1, whose observed defection is strong evidence of selfishness; report elevated suspicion of P5 for the same reason and lower probabilities for observed cooperators.
Choose C with P7, who previously cooperated; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare when both are good.
Cooperate with likely-good P10 to maximize good players’ combined payoff; their prior cooperation is evidence against selfishness.
Cooperate with P8, whose prior cooperation supports coordination and good-player welfare. Use observed actions as evidence about roles, while treating reports as uncertain.
Cooperate with P9, who previously cooperated with me; mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare. P1’s observed defection remains strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with P3, whose observed cooperation supports good-player coordination. Treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness; prior cooperators are unlikely selfish.

Cooperate with P5, whose prior cooperation is evidence they are good; defecting would reduce total good-player payoff if P5 is good. P1’s reported and P7’s observed defections raise their selfishness probabilities.
Cooperate with P6, whose observed cooperation and consistent coordination messages strongly suggest they will cooperate; this maximizes the good players’ joint payoff.
Defect against P4 based on their observed defection and high selfishness probability; in the final round, this protects good-player payoff if P4 is selfish.

As a selfish player, I defected in every round to maximize my payoff. I treated observed cooperation against my defection as evidence that a player is good; the remaining players who defected remain uncertain.

Cooperated with untested and observed cooperators to support shared good-player payoffs; defected against P1 after its observed defection. Updated private identity beliefs using encounters and treated public claims as unverified.
Cooperated to support shared good-player welfare, while using observed actions to assess others; P1’s defection was the only observed defection.

Generally cooperated to preserve gains for good players. Updated beliefs from encounters: P1’s defection and P10’s later exploitation raised suspicion; cooperation by others lowered it somewhat. Treated public claims as uncertain.

Cooperated with most opponents to support good-player welfare, using observed actions to update role beliefs. Treated defection as strong evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence favoring good, while recognizing actions do not prove roles.

Cooperated throughout to support shared welfare among good players. P1’s observed defection is strong, but not conclusive, evidence of selfishness; the others’ observed cooperation supports low selfishness probabilities.
Cooperated with observed cooperators to support good-player coordination; treated P1’s reported and observed defections as evidence of selfishness, while keeping other role beliefs cautious.

Cooperated with observed cooperators and untested players to support good-player payoffs; defected when evidence suggested an opponent was selfish. Updated role beliefs from observed actions and credible reports.

P1.strategy: As a selfish player, I defected in every round to maximize my payoff. I treated observed cooperation against my defection as evidence that a player is good; the remaining players who defected remain uncertain.

P2.strategy: Cooperated with untested and observed cooperators to support shared good-player payoffs; defected against P1 after its observed defection. Updated private identity beliefs using encounters and treated public claims as unverified.

P3.strategy: Cooperated to support shared good-player welfare, while using observed actions to assess others; P1’s defection was the only observed defection.

P4.strategy: Generally cooperated to preserve gains for good players. Updated beliefs from encounters: P1’s defection and P10’s later exploitation raised suspicion; cooperation by others lowered it somewhat. Treated public claims as uncertain.

P5.strategy: Cooperated with most opponents to support good-player welfare, using observed actions to update role beliefs. Treated defection as strong evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence favoring good, while recognizing actions do not prove roles.

P6.strategy: Cooperated throughout to support shared welfare among good players. P1’s observed defection is strong, but not conclusive, evidence of selfishness; the others’ observed cooperation supports low selfishness probabilities.

P7.strategy: Cooperated with observed cooperators to support good-player coordination; treated P1’s reported and observed defections as evidence of selfishness, while keeping other role beliefs cautious.

P8.strategy: Cooperated with observed cooperators and untested players to support good-player payoffs; defected when evidence suggested an opponent was selfish. Updated role beliefs from observed actions and credible reports.
